semantics.function: out equals the bit of in indexed by sel, for every selection from 0 through 255
semantics.evidence: Original problem says sel=0 selects in[0], sel=1 selects in[1], sel=2 selects in[2], etc., and calls this a 256-to-1 multiplexer.
semantics.timing: Combinational selection; no clock, reset, state, or added latency is specified or present in the interface.
semantics.initialization: No initialization requirement or stored state; output follows current inputs.

numeric.selection: Unsigned 8-bit index covers all 256 input bits; no arithmetic or overflow.
numeric.bit_order: Index zero is the least significant vector bit.

verification.oracle: Independent scan of all 256 positions to find the position equal to sel.
verification.cases: All selections on zero and one vectors, every one-hot input against all selections, complementary one-cold patterns, alternating patterns and selected X/Z data.
verification.sampling: Sample after a one-time-unit combinational settling delay following input changes; no cycle or reset sampling applies.
verification.completion: Bounded timeout, fatal mismatches, and PASS only after all cases complete.

specification_ambiguities: Unknown or high-impedance selector behavior is unspecified; use normal Verilog indexed bit-select semantics and do not impose additional requirements.
